text_en:
حدثني زيد بن علي عن آبائه عن علي بن أبي طالب عليهم السلام قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وطئ بعر بعير رطب فمسحه بالارض وصلى ولم يحدث وضوءا ولم"
"Zayd ibn Ali narrated to me from his fathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stepping on wet camel dung, so he wiped it with the ground and prayed, and did not perform wudu, nor...
He washes the foot.

Zaid narrated from Abu Khalid, who said: 'The Qils invalidates wudu.' He said, 'I asked Zayd about the Qibla invalidating wudu,' and he said, 'It does not invalidate wudu except by impurity. And this is not an impurity.' He said, 'I asked Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) about a man eating camel meat or sheep meat; does that invalidate his wudu?' He said, 'No.' And he said, 'Indeed, wudu is from that etiquette.'

Nassr ibn Muzahim narrated to me, who said: Ibrahim ibn al-Zubairqan narrated to me, who said: Abu Khalid Amr ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to me from Zayd ibn Ali from his father from his grandfather from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: 'The bath for major impurity is obligatory. And the washing of a dead person is recommended. If you purify yourself, it suffices for you. And the bath for cupping is [obligatory]. If you purify yourself, it suffices for you. And the bath of the two Eids and what I love to leave them. And the bath of Friday, and what I love to leave it because I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: "Whoever comes on Friday, let him take a bath.'

Abd al-Aziz ibn Ishaq ibn Ja'far ibn al-Haitham al-Qadi al-Baghdadi narrated from Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nakha'i al-Kufi, who said: 'Narrated from Sulayman ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubayd al-Maharbi, who said: Narrated to me Nasr ibn Muzahim al-Mungiri al-'Attar, who said: Narrated to me Ibrahim ibn al-Zubayqan al-Taimi, who said: Narrated to me Abu Khalid al-Wasiti, may Allah have mercy on him. He said: Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, asked about a man who forgets to wipe his head until his wudu dries. (He replied): He repeats wiping his head, and it suffices for him; he does not repeat his wudu. (And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said): Istinja' is an emphasized Sunnah, and it is not permissible to leave it unless one cannot find water. (And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said): Siwak (mouth rinsing) and istinshaq (nose blowing) are a Sunnah, and they are not like Istinja'. (And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said): It is not permissible to leave the siwak and istinshaq in Ghusl al-Janabah. He said: And it is fine to perform wudu with the water of menstruation. The one who has Janabah is not menstruating; and Janabah in the hand is only where Allah Almighty has made it. (And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said): It is not permissible to perform wudu with water that a dog has licked or seven [things]. (And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said): It is fine with the water of the cat, sheep, camel, and horse. As for the mule and donkey, if they have saliva, one should not perform wudu with their water; and if they do not have saliva, it suffices to perform wudu with it, even if you are unaware whether or not they have saliva, leaving it is better unless you find otherwise. (And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said): It is not permissible to perform wudu with milk or wine, whether sweet or strong. And one cannot perform wudu except with water, as Allah Almighty has said: (Water is pure). Abu Khalid narrated that he asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, what invalidates wudu. He said: Excrement, urine, wind, nosebleed, vomiting, blood, pus, and sleeping while lying down. Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said: It is fine to perform wudu with the water of the bathhouse. (And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said): If one steps on something from animal droppings while it is moist, wash it; and if it is dry, there is no harm in it. He said: And horses, mules, and donkeys are equal in this regard. Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said: It was permissible regarding the meat of horses, but he disliked their droppings and urine. (He said): It is fine with the urine of sheep, camels, cows, and what whose meat is eaten touches the garment. (He said): It is not permissible for a woman to wipe over her khimar; if she wipes on the front of her head, it suffices. (He said): Regarding blood that touches the garment: If it is less than a dirham, there is no harm in it, and washing it would be better. If it is more than the measure of a dirham, wash it. Abu Khalid narrated that he said:

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'When the two foreskins meet and the prepuce is covered, then Ghusl becomes obligatory, whether it has descended or not.'

Abu Khalid narrated to me, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: I asked Zaid, peace be upon him, about the Ghusl from Janabah, and he said: You wash your hands three times, then you perform Istinja, and you perform Wudu' like your Wudu' for Salat, then you wash your head three times, then you pour water over the rest of your body three times, then you wash your feet.

And he descended and said Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, 'How is the boundary established, and how is the washing not established?' He said, 'I asked Zayd, peace be upon him, about the woman who sees nocturnal emission in a dream. She performs Ghusl (ritual bath).' And Zayd ibn Ali said, peace be upon him, regarding the man who feels wetness but does not see a vision. He said, 'If it is warm water, he performs Ghusl.' I asked him, peace be upon him, about semen that stains the garment. He said, 'He washes little of it and much of it.' And [regarding] urine and feces, he washes little of it and much of it.

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'The woman in menstruation and the impure person who is menstruating and impure both sweat on the garment.' He said: 'Menstruation and impurity are where Allah Almighty has placed them, so they do not wash their garments.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, who said: 'I was a man with discharge; I was ashamed to ask the Messenger of Allah about it because of my daughter's status. So Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad ordered him and asked him, saying: "O Miqdad, there are three matters: the *wadi* is something that follows urine like semen, so that is pure from it and no washing is due; and the *madhi* if you see something or remember it and it spreads, so that is pure from it and no washing is due; and the *manī* is the flowing liquid when it falls with desire, and a bath (ghusl) is obligatory." Zaid narrated that Imam Zayd ibn Ali said: "It is better for the person in ritual impurity to urinate before he performs Ghusl, and if he does not do so, the Ghusl suffices him.
And Zayd ibn Ali said, peace be upon him, regarding cupping that it invalidates wudu and washes its places; if one performs ghusl, it is better.

Zayd narrated from his father, who narrated from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, shook hands with Hudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! I am in a state of major impurity (janabah).' The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to him: 'The Muslim is not impure.'

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: 'We were commanded in the Ghusl for Janabah for the man with a sa' and for the woman with a sa' and a half.' Zayd (may Allah bless him) said: 'We used to measure the Wudu for Salat by a mud, and the mud was two riṭlān.' Abu Khalid said:

Hadith narrated from Zayd ibn Ali's father, from Juhd, from Ali (peace be upon him): The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked whether the menstruating woman should feed before she performs Ghusl. He said: No, not until she performs Ghusl or performs Wudu for prayer.

Abu Khalid said: Zayd ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'It is permissible to have intercourse and then repeat it before performing wudu.' And I asked Zayd ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, about rainwater. He said: 'There is no harm in it; the earth purifies some of itself by others.'
The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'A woman should not use anything for purification except water, unless she cannot find water.'
Narrated to me by Zayd ibn Ali from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'The torment of the grave is from three things: urine, debt, and backbiting.'

A man who stands in the middle of the night to brush his teeth, and then purifies himself for salat, and performs wudu with perfection, and then goes to one of the houses of Allah, may he be glorified, a malak comes to him and places his mouth on it. Nothing leaves his mouth except that it enters the mouth of the angel until the Day of Judgment, when he will come with it as a witness and an intercessor.

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: 'No prayer is accepted except with zakat, and no prayer is accepted except with Quran, and no prayer is accepted except with purity, and no charity is accepted from embezzlement.'

Zayd narrated from his father, who narrated from his grandfather, and from Ali, peace be upon him, that if he entered the exit, he should say: 'Bismillah, O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the impure impurity and the foul.' And when he exited the exit, he should say: 'Praise be to Allah Who has restored my body, praise be to Allah who removed the harm from me.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'I was given three things that no prophet before me was given. I was given the Earth as a mosque and for purification.' Allah Almighty said: 'If you do not find water, then perform tayammum with clean earth, and lawful to me is the spoils, and it is not lawful to anyone before me.' His saying, Exalted is Allah, 'And know that what you have gained from anything, then belongs to Allah's fifth, and for the Messenger, and for the relatives.' The verse [referring to] the support by terror over a distance of one month, and I was favored over the prophets, peace be upon them, on the Day of Judgment with three things. My Ummah will come on the Day of Judgment adorned, purified from the traces of wudu', known among nations. And the mu'adhdhin will come on the Day of Judgment with the longest necks, calling the testimony that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. And the third [thing] is not for any prophet, which is that he will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment for my sin, due to His saying, 'Allah forgives you what passed from your sin and what is yet to come.'
I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about wudu repeatedly. He said: 'It is permissible, and the three [times] are best.'

Zayd ibn Ali narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'No Muslim performs wudu, then says when he finishes his wudu: Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilaika. O Allah, make me among those who repent, and make me among the purified, and forgive me, for indeed You are over all things powerful.'

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wiped before the descent of the Ma'idah, and when the verse of the Ma'idah descended, he did not wipe after it."

"The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs [the act] out of a good deed, then that good deed is for him.'
I am the son of Fatima, peace be upon her. We do not wipe over the khuffayn, nor the 'imamah, nor the kummah, nor the khimar, nor the jihaz.
Zaid narrated from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: 'If a man has sores, or smallpox, or wounds on him, then pour water over them.'

Zaid narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: 'He performed wudu and wiped his feet, and he said this is wudu for one who has not been informed. I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about the wudu of a pagan. He said: He performs wudu with the water from what he drank, and he does not perform wudu with the water of his ablution unless he knows that he drank intoxicants or ate pork. So he does not perform wudu with the water of his drinking nor his wudu.' I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about backbiting and slander nullifying wudu. He said: No. And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, regarding the vessel in which a beetle dies, shouting, and discord, he said: It does not harm you. I asked Zayd about a man who performs wudu twice, twice. He said: It suffices for him. I said: But if he performs wudu once, once? He said: It suffices for him. And I asked Zayd, peace be upon him, about a man who performs wudu and then cuts his nails. He said: The water passes over his nails.

Let me tell you, Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, from his fathers, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: 'If a man has visible sores that he cannot bathe with them, let him perform the wudu of his prayer and pour water over it.'
Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: 'The Book preceded the two skins.'

Zaid narrated from an unnamed companion, who said: 'He was told that a man had smallpox and had become impure [janabah]. So how should we treat him?' He was told to wash him. I asked Zayd, peace be upon him, about the traveler who fears for himself from snow. Is it permissible for him to wipe over his socks? He said: 'Yes, this is an excuse like wiping over splints. If he is able to perform Ghusl, then wiping is not sufficient.' And I asked Zayd, peace be upon him, about a man whose discharge runs continuously. He said: 'He should perform Wudu for every prayer.'

Narrated to me by Zayd ibn Ali from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'If you are on a journey and you have water with you, and you fear thirst, then perform tayammum and keep the water for yourself.'
Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said: 'Tayammum is two strikes: one for the face and one for the forearms up to the elbows.'

Zaid narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: 'If a well contains an object—be it a small piece of wood, or dung, or a bird—he should draw forty *sa'* of water. If the water has changed, he should draw the water until it becomes pure. I asked, 'If a chicken, pigeon, or cat falls into it and dies, but the water does not change?' He said, 'Draw one hundred *sa'* from it.' I asked, 'If the water changes?' He said, 'Draw until it becomes pure.' Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, mentioned regarding the well that urine, blood, or wine drips into it; he should draw all its water. Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, also mentioned regarding the Great Pool and the vast pond that nothing can pollute its water, and concerning running water that nothing can pollute it.

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said: 'In the case of being in a state where water is not found, he performs tayammum and prays. If he finds water, he performs ghusl and does not repeat the prayer.' He said: And Zaid ibn Ali, peace be upon them, said: He performs tayammum for every prayer and prays with every tayammum his obligatory and supererogatory prayers.

"Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'The one who performs tayammum cannot lead those who perform wudu and the absolute ones [who are not in a state of necessity].' Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And everything you perform tayammum with from the earth is sufficient for you.' Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) said regarding the one who performs tayammum finding water during prayer, [he should] face the prayer. I asked Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) about a man who is traveling in a muddy area of clay and has not found water. He said: 'He performs tayammum from the dust of his saddlebag or the dung of his donkey or the dust of his garment, and the ruling for the man and the woman in tayammum are equal.' I asked Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) about a menstruating woman purifying herself while traveling. He said: 'She performs tayammum, and if she finds water, she performs ghusl, and nothing of her prayer is invalidated.' And Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for him to have intercourse while he is traveling and performing tayammum.'

He narrated to me, Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'A woman came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, claiming that she was purging blood.' The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Curse Satan! This is a rush from Satan in your womb. So do not perform salat for it.' She asked, 'How shall I act, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Perform [your] days when you used to menstruate every month; do not perform salat nor fast, and do not enter the mosque nor recite the Qur'an. And when your days come that you used to menstruate, make it the last of your menstruation days. Perform ghusl for Fajr, then enter the *kirsif* (uterus) and perform *istithfar* (the purification/bleeding assessment) of a man. Then pray Fajr. Then [do so] again at Dhuhr until the last time, perform ghusl, enter the *kirsif*, and perform *istithfar* of a man. Then pray Dhuhr when the first time of Asr has entered. Pray Asr. Then [do so] again for Maghrib until the last time. Then perform ghusl, enter the *kirsif*, and perform *istithfar* of a man. Then pray Maghrib when the first time of Isha has entered. Then pray Isha.' She said, 'So I can't bear it,' while crying to him. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, separated [the ruling for] her, and said: 'Perform ghusl for every purity that you used to do, and consider it as the wound in your body. Whenever blood flows, perform a purification. And do not leave the *kirsif* and *istithfar*; if this lasts for her, then she may enter the mosque, recite the Qur'an, pray salat, and perform the rituals.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'If the menstruating woman becomes pure before Maghrib, she makes up Dhuhr and Asr. And if she becomes pure before Fajr, she makes up Maghrib and Isha.'

Ubayd narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubayd, who said: 'Nusr ibn Muzahim al-Mungari narrated to me, and he said: Ibraheem ibn al-Zubairaqan al-Tymi narrated to me, and he said: Abu Khalid Amr ibn Khalid al-Wasiti said:

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon him, who said: 'The Adhan is recited in pairs, the Iqamah is recited in pairs, and it is chanted in the Adhan and lowered in the Iqamah.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'There are three things that one cannot leave unless he is incapable: a man who hears the muezzin and does not say what he says; a man who attends a funeral and does not greet its people; and [a man] who reaches the Imam while he is prostrating, does not say takbir, and then prostrates with them, and it is not counted.'
It is not upon the women to give the call to prayer (adhan) nor to perform the Iqamah.

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, came to him. A man said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah, I do not love you for the sake of Allah." He said, "But rather I hate you for the sake of Allah." He asked, "Why? Because you sing with your call to prayer," meaning he makes it melodious and takes payment for teaching the Quran. And he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, say: 'Whoever takes payment for teaching the Quran, his portion on the Day of Judgment is...' Zaid ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'The call to prayer is in the five daily prayers and on Friday, but there is no call to prayer or Iqama on the two Eids, nor is there a call to prayer or Iqama on Witr.' And Zaid ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'If you are traveling, call for Fajr and establish [the prayer] for the rest of the prayers.' And Zaid ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'It is not permissible for a boy or a woman to give the call to prayer for men.' And Zaid [Ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'If you are in your place, their calling will compensate you, and if you call it, it is better.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'Gabriel descended upon the Prophet, peace be upon him, when the sun was at its zenith, and he commanded him to perform Dhuhr salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him when it was the height of the afternoon, and he commanded him to perform Asr salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him when the solar disc fell, and he commanded him to perform Maghrib salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him when twilight occurred, and he commanded him to perform Isha salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him when dawn appeared, and he commanded him to perform Fajr salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him from the next day when it was at the zenith from Dhuhr, so he commanded him to perform Dhuhr salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him when it was at two heights from Dhuhr, so he commanded him to perform Asr salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him when the disc fell, and he commanded him to perform Maghrib salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him after the passing of a third of the night, and he commanded him to perform Isha salat. Then Gabriel descended upon him [when dawn broke], so he commanded him to perform Fajr salat. Then he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the time between these two times?' I heard Imam Al-Shahid Abu Al-Hussein Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) when he was asked about His saying, Exalted is He: "Establish prayer from the zenith of the sun to the darkness of night and the recitation of dawn." So he said (may Allah be pleased with him): 'The zenith of the sun means its noon point, and the darkness of night is its third part when the whiteness leaves the bottom of the sky, and the recitation of dawn that it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.' And Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'The best times are the first one, and if you delay it, there is no harm.' And Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'The red twilight.'
Narrated to me by Zayd ibn Ali from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'When the muezzin says "The prayer has begun," say *takbir* and do not wait.'

Zaid bin Ali narrated from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon him), who said: 'The key to prayer's purity and its prohibition is the Takbir, and its dissolution is the Taslim. And Zaid bin Ali said: If he catches the Imam while he is bowing, let him say one Takbir for entering the prayer, then bow his parts; that will suffice.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'He used to exaggerate in raising and lowering, and Zayd said that he used to exaggerate in every raising and lowering. And Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The first takbir is obligatory, and the rest of the takbir is Sunnah." And Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Is *subh* or *hal* considered within the prayer?" And Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "A man is not considered within the prayer except by a takbir."

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'He used to recite in the first two units of Maghrib and Isha and Fajr, and he used to recite in the first two units of Dhuhr and Asr, and he used to say *subhanAllah* in the last two units of Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha, and the last rak'ah of Maghrib.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'When he began the salat, he would say: Allahu Akbar; I direct my face to Him Who created the heavens and the earth in a straight manner, [a] Muslim. And I am not of the polytheists. My prayer, my worship, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. By that have I been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. I seek refuge with Allah from Satan.' Then he would begin and recite.
Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'Every prayer without recitation is a deception.'
Zayd narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'He used to recite Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Raheem aloud.'

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: 'They used to recite behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and grace be upon him. So the Prophet, peace and grace be upon him, said: "You have mixed up things, so do not do it." Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: I prayed Maghrib behind my father (peace be upon him). He forgot Al-Fatihah in the first rak'ah, so he recited it in the second and performed the prostration of forgetfulness.'

Zayd narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: 'If a man enters salat and forgets to recite until he bows down, let him stand up, then recite, then bow down and perform two prostrations of forgetfulness. Zayd said: It is not permissible for one to interrupt the Imam in salat, even if he does so, the prayer is complete. And Zayd said: The Mu'awwidhatayn are from the Qur'an. And Zayd said: Whoever hears with his ear shall not be interrupted.'

And it was Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying in the Tashahhud of the first two rak'ahs: 'Bismillah, walhamdulillah, wa al-asma'ul husna kulluha lillah. Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh.' Then he rises. It was Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) who used to extend his right foot and spread his left one. He said: And Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Prayer is not accepted without Tashahhud.'

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'He used to pause in Fajr before bowing and in Witr after bowing. Then he paused in Kufa during Witr before bowing. And Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) used to pause in Fajr and Witr before bowing.'

Zayd narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: 'He used to recite at dawn this verse: Believing in Allah and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the nations. And what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord, until the end of the verse.'

My father narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'My Ummah will not be kept safe from affliction as long as they do not show the characteristics of dealing in usury (Riba), or showing bribery, or cutting off kinship ties, or abandoning Salat in congregation, and if this house is left to be led, then they will not argue.'

I was narrated to by Zayd ibn Ali from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: 'There is no prayer for the neighbor of the mosque who does not respond to the call when he hears it.'

He narrated to me Zayd ibn Ali from his father, from his grandfather, who said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, saying: Under the shade of the Throne on the Day when there will be no shade except His shade, a man left his house and performed wudu, then walked to one of the houses of Allah to perform an obligation among the obligations of Allah Almighty. He perished in what was between him and that, and a man who stood in the middle of the night after the eyes had rested, so he performed purification, then stood to one of the houses of Allah, might Allah magnify Him, and he perished in what was between him and that.'

Malik said: I visited Abu al-Darda, and I found him in the morning, meaning he was sleeping. So he said, 'O Abu al-Darda.' He said, 'It was something from me during the night, so I slept.' I was ill, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, visited me. He said, 'Say: O Allah, I ask You for the promptness of my wellness, patience regarding my affliction, and a release into Your mercy.' So I said it, and I rose as if I had been revived from a yoke.

He narrated to me, Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: 'The reward is according to the calamity; whoever is afflicted with a calamity, let him mention his calamity because you will not be afflicted with what I was afflicted with.'

I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about a woman praying in the middle of the row. He said: 'The prayer of one who is on her right and on her left, and from behind her, is ruined.' He said: 'If he is on the Imam, he performs a nosebleed (bleeding from the nose) for the residents, so he leads them in the rest of the prayer of the traveler, then he leads a man from the travelers, and they greet him, then the residents rise and complete what remains of their prayer. I asked Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) about a man who greets him during prayer and forgets, so he returns the greeting. He said: 'His prayer is invalidated.' It is not in the camels, the carriers and the loaded ones, charity.

Ibrahim ibn al-Subzurqan al-Taimi narrated to us, Abu Khalid Amr ibn Khalid al-Wasiti, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: 'There is no charity in less than five years of camels. When it reaches five, there is one sheep in it. Then nothing in it. When it reaches ten, there are two sheep in it. When it reaches fifteen, there are three sheep in it. When it reaches twenty, there are four sheep in it. When it reaches twenty-five, there are five sheep in it. If it increases by one, there is a female calf in it. If it is not a female calf, then a male foal, which is older than it by a year, up to thirty-five years. When it increases by one on thirty-five, there is a female foal up to forty-five. If it increases by one on forty-five, there is a mare up to sixty. If it increases by one on sixty, there is a colt up to seventy-five. If it increases by one on seventy-five, there are two foals up to ninety. If it increases by one on ninety, there are two mares and the stallion up to two hundred. If the camels increase, then in every fifty, there is a mare.'

Zaid narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'There is nothing in less than forty sheep of the flock; if it is forty, then there is one sheep to two hundred and one; if it exceeds two hundred and one, then there are two sheep to two hundred; and if it exceeds two hundred by one, then there are three sheep to three hundred; and if it exceeds three hundred, there is nothing in the excess until it reaches four hundred; and when it reaches four hundred, there are four sheep; so if the flock increases, in every hundred sheep, there is one sheep.'

It is not a charity for what is less than two hundred dirhams of paper; but when it reaches two hundred, there are five dirhams in it, and if it exceeds that, it is by calculation. And it is not a charity for what is less than twenty mithqals; but when it reaches twenty mithqals, there is half a mithqal in it, and what exceeds that is by calculation."

"The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and works righteous deeds, then he will enter Paradise.'

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'There is no zakat in the money that you benefit from until a full lunar year passes over it since you received it. If a full lunar year passes over it, then give its zakat.'
Abu Ubayda narrated from Jabir ibn Zayd, from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: 'Actions are judged by intentions.'
It is not due zakat on land of ten measures of dates, nor raisins, nor wheat, nor barley, nor grain, until the kind reaches five *awsaq*. One *wasaq* is sixty *saa'*.

He narrated to me Zayd ibn Ali from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: 'If I buy a measure of food for a hundred dirhams, I gather on it a group of my brothers. It is better to me than if I go to your market and buy a slave and free him.'

He narrated from 'Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'Whoever lends a loan that has an equivalent for it, it is charity. He said (upon him), I asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, yesterday,' and he said, 'Whoever lends a loan that has an equivalent for it, it is charity.' And I said today, 'Whoever lends a loan that has an equivalent for it, every day it is charity.' He said (peace be upon him): Yes, whoever lends a loan and delays it after its due time, it is for him every day its equivalent in charity.

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'Prayer is not completed except with zakat, and prayer is not completed except with purity, and charity is not accepted if it is from embezzlement.'
Three of the characteristics of the prophets, peace be upon them, are: delaying the breaking of the fast, delaying the pre-dawn meal, and placing a hand on another's hand below the navel.
O Allah, for You we fasted and by Your sustenance we broke our fast; accept it from us.

And Zayd ibn Ali narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: 'Three things do not break the fast for the fasting person: vomiting, drawing [blood], and nocturnal emission.' And Zayd ibn Ali said: 'Cupping and kohl do not break the fast for the fasting person, and I dislike cupping due to fear of weakness.' He narrated to me Zayd ibn Ali from his father, from his grandfather, who said: 'In the sick person and the traveler, they fast in the month of Ramadan, then they make up [the missed days]. X narrated from Y, from Z, who said...

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: 'When a group came and testified that they fasted upon seeing the new crescent and that they had completed thirty days, Ali (peace be upon him) said: "We did not fast except for twenty-eight days." As for (the oath of vain talk), it is when a man swears by an affair while he thinks that it is as he swore; so there is no expiation nor sin in that. This is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah will not hold you accountable for what you utter in your faith, but He will hold you accountable for what you contract in your faith.' As for (the oath of adornment), it is when a man swears that he will not do an affair from among affairs, and then he does it; upon him is the expiation for that, as Allah Almighty said: 'Feeding ten poor people from what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave.' For whoever cannot find [it], then fasting three consecutive days. This is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah has decreed for you the adornment of your faith, and Allah is your protector; He is the All-Knowing, the Wise.'

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: 'He feeds them in the morning and in the evening half a sa' of barley or sough or flour, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of barley. He feeds them in the morning and in the evening.'"

"The Prophet narrated from Abu Huraira, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'O people! I am giving you advice, so take it seriously.' "

I created you from the clay of 'Ali's people, and I created your Shia from you. If they were to strike their necks with swords, they would increase for you nothing but fragrance.' I said: 'O Lord, and who is the eldest companion?' He said: 'Your brother Ali ibn Abi Talib.' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, gave me good tidings of it, and my sons Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn from her, and that was before the Hijra by three epochs.'

My master, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded me to fight the oath-breakers, the unjust ones, and the rebels. So I did not leave anything that my beloved Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded me with.

He said: I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about the ghusl of the menstruating and postpartum woman; he, peace be upon him, said: like the ghusl from janaba. I said: if he swore not to eat this fresh date and it became a dry date and he ate from it? He, peace be upon him, said: he breaks [the oath]. I said: what is the difference between these two — the paste from the date and the dry date from the fresh date? He, peace be upon him, said: because the paste from the date is by conversion and change. Do you not see that if he swore not to speak to this man and he spoke to a son of his born afterward, he does not break [the oath], for he is from him; and likewise if he swore not to eat this ewe and it bore a kid and he ate from it, he does not break [the oath], for it is from her — this resembles the paste. But if he swore not to speak to this boy and he became a man and he spoke to him, he breaks [the oath]; and if he swore not to eat this lamb and it became a ram and he ate from it, he breaks [the oath] — this in aspect resembles the fresh date, for this is not by conversion. He said: a woman asked the Commander of the Faithful Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, and said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, I swore I would not eat from the milk of a ewe of mine, then I made of it clarified butter (samn) and ate from it; he, peace be upon him, said: there is no breaking [of the oath] upon you. He said: and butter and shiraz? He, peace be upon him, said: he breaks [the oath]; and he said: butter and shiraz are not [by] conversion, but clarified butter is conversion. I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about a man who swore not to eat dry dates and ate fresh dates, or swore not to eat fresh dates and ate dry dates, or swore not to eat milk and ate shiraz or clarified butter or butter or cheese; he, peace be upon him, said: he does not break [the oath] in any of that, for swearing off a thing by its specific self and a thing not by its specific self differ. He said: I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about a boy who swears while he is a boy then reaches puberty and breaks [the oath]; he, peace be upon him, said: nothing is upon him; and likewise the disbeliever who swears then accepts Islam and breaks [the oath], he, peace be upon him, said: nothing is upon him — Islam demolishes what came before it. And Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said: the import of people's oaths is according to what they intend and resolve; so if they have no intention, then carry that upon the language of their land and what they customarily understand, and do not carry it upon what they disavow.

Zayd ibn Ali narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, forbade the sale of muhafala and muzabana, and the sale of trees until they set [fruit], and the sale of dates until they ripen — meaning they turn yellow or red. Imam Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said: the sale of muzabana is selling dates for dates; muhaqala is selling standing crop for wheat; and al-izha is the yellowing and reddening. I asked Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, about a man who buys the fruit before it matures on condition that he cut it; he, peace be upon him, said: there is no harm in that. I said: but if he buys it before it matures on condition that he leave it until it matures? He, peace be upon him, said: this is not lawful and is not permissible.

Zaid narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, forbade the selling of *mahāfilah*, *muzābanah*, and the selling of trees before they are ready, and the selling of dates before they ripen. I asked Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) about a man buying fruit before it reaches maturity so that he cuts it; he said: 'It is permissible to do so.' I said: If he buys it before it reaches maturity so that he leaves it until it ripens? He said: 'This is not lawful and not permissible.'
